hide_smoke_curing.observation: Hides pegged out, scraped clean and hung in the smoke of a smouldering fire stay supple and no longer rot.

ground_stone_axes.observation: An axe ground smooth on sandstone and water bites deep, rarely shatters, and can be reground for a lifetime.

warp_weighted_looms.social_consequence: Cloth becomes a household's wealth and a woman's work of years; it is given at marriages and hoarded against hard times.

burnished_slipped_wares.observation: A pot rubbed with a smooth pebble before firing, or dipped in fine slip, holds water without sweating and shines like stone.

painted_pottery.observation: Red and black earth paints fired onto the pot keep their colour, and each village's patterns can be told apart.

native_copper_working.observation: Lumps of red metal found in the green rock can be hammered into awls and beads, and heated again when they grow brittle.

tournette.observation: A slow turning disc lets the potter smooth the rim and paint bands all the way round in one steady pass.

horizontal_ground_loom.observation: Warp pegged between two beams on the ground lets two weavers work a wide cloth side by side.

copper_smelting.social_consequence: Metal no longer depends on lucky finds of native copper; those who know the green ores and the fire gain a new kind of wealth.

fire_setting_mining.observation: A fire built against the rock face, then doused, cracks the ore so stone mauls can break it loose.

lead_smelting.production_contract: Galena, charcoal and furnace work produce refined lead and silver-bearing bullion; fumes and slag stay with the smelting site.

seed_oil_pressing.production_contract: Seed or olive stock, a press and work produce lamp and leather oil; the press cake remains as fodder.

reduction_firing.observation: Choking the kiln with green wood at the end of the firing turns the pot black, and the potters learn to do it on purpose.

wool_spinning.observation: The new woolly sheep are plucked each spring, and the fleece spins into a warm, springy yarn that linen cannot match.

arsenical_copper.observation: Copper smelted from certain grey-streaked ores comes out harder and casts cleaner, though its fumes smell of garlic.
arsenical_copper.social_consequence: Harder copper blades are prized and traded far; smiths who know the ores gain rank, and some of them sicken from the fumes.

lost_wax_casting.observation: A figure modelled in beeswax, coated in clay and baked, leaves a perfect hollow for the metal to fill.
lost_wax_casting.social_consequence: Intricate cast figures, maceheads and fittings become marks of rank and gifts between rulers.

sheet_copper_riveting.observation: Copper beaten into sheet and joined with copper rivets makes vessels and panels too large to cast.

faience.observation: Crushed quartz bound with a little natron and fired forms its own blue-green glaze, bright as turquoise.
faience.social_consequence: Glazed beads and amulets become a sought-after trade good, and the secret of the blue is guarded.

wheel_thrown_pottery.observation: A heavy wheel spun fast lets a potter lift a pot from a lump of clay in the time it takes to say a prayer.
wheel_thrown_pottery.social_consequence: Pots are thrown by the hundred by full-time men at the wheel; household potting fades and pottery becomes a trade.

mould_made_bowls.observation: Coarse bowls pressed over a mould by the thousand all hold the same ration, and are thrown away when broken.

tube_drilled_stone_vessels.observation: A reed or copper tube spun on wet sand slowly bores out a vessel from the hardest stone.

silver_cupellation.social_consequence: Silver becomes the measure of wealth and debt; temples and rulers hoard it and weigh it out.

bivalve_moulds.observation: Two matching stone halves bound together let the smith cast an axe with its shaft-hole already in it.

meteoric_iron_working.observation: The black metal fallen from the sky can be cold-hammered into beads, rarer than gold and buried with the great.

lampblack_capture.production_contract: Lamp soot collected from oil or resin flames is gathered as a black pigment for paint and ink; it needs fuel and tending.

temple_workshops.observation: Under the temple's overseer, weavers, smiths and carpenters work from its stores and deliver to its storerooms.
temple_workshops.social_consequence: The temple becomes the largest employer and the largest owner of goods; craftwork answers to its overseers.

copper_carpentry_tools.observation: Copper saws fed with sand cut stone, and copper chisels cut true mortises in timber that flint could only bruise.

tin_smelting.production_contract: Cassiterite, charcoal and furnace work produce refined tin; tin ore is rare, so most tin must be found far off or traded for.

bronze_alloying.social_consequence: Bronze needs tin from far away; whoever controls the tin routes controls tools and weapons, and wars follow the trade.

closed_moulds.observation: A mould closed on all sides casts both faces of a blade at once, and every casting from it is the same.

wool_felting_fulling.observation: Wool trodden in hot water and soap-root shrinks into dense felt for cloaks, hats and tent walls.

goldsmith_filigree.observation: Gold drawn into thread and fine grains is soldered into patterns so delicate they seem woven.
goldsmith_filigree.social_consequence: Jewellery of gold and silver marks the ruler's house and the temple; goldsmiths work for the palace alone.

hard_soldering.observation: A solder of gold and copper melts just before the metal it joins, so fine parts can be fixed without melting them.

bronze_work_hardening.observation: Hammering a cast bronze edge cold makes it harder and keener than the casting alone.

pot_bellows.observation: Two clay pots covered with hide and worked by the feet blow a steady blast that no team of blowpipes can match.
pot_bellows.social_consequence: Paired bellows keep the hearth white-hot; one smelt yields more metal for less charcoal, and metal grows cheaper.

cored_socket_casting.observation: A clay core set in the mould leaves a socket in the casting, so a spearhead or axe fits its shaft without a hole being drilled.

palace_weaving_houses.observation: Hundreds of women and children weave in the palace workshops, drawing wool and rations by the month and delivering cloth by weight.
palace_weaving_houses.social_consequence: Cloth is made for the palace on a vast scale and exported; the weavers are rationed dependants, not free households.

weighed_alloy_recipes.observation: The smith weighs out copper and tin by the shekel, one part to so many, and writes the proportion down.

raised_bronze_vessels.observation: A bronze disc hammered round and round over a stake rises into a bowl, a cauldron, a helmet.

standard_ingots.observation: Copper is cast into ingots of a fixed weight and shape, so a load of metal can be counted rather than weighed.

shaft_furnaces.observation: A tall clay shaft with blast pipes set low smelts a whole basket of ore in one firing, and the slag runs out below.
shaft_furnaces.social_consequence: Metal comes by the load instead of the handful; smelting sites become industrial, smoky places that strip the hills of wood.

alum_mordant_dyeing.observation: Wool boiled first in alum water takes madder and weld deep and fast, and the colour no longer washes out.

ceramic_glaze_formulation.social_consequence: Glazed jars keep oil and wine without seeping; fine glazed wares become a mark of a well-off household.

core_formed_glass.social_consequence: Glass flasks for scented oil are among the costliest things a household can own, and the palace controls their making.

tapestry_weaving.observation: Weft of many colours beaten in patch by patch on the upright loom builds figures and scenes into the cloth.
